<reason>CON won by making the motion as written harder to defend than PRO’s civic-standing frame could repair. PRO’s best case—hosts already pay in congestion, so a share should be sequenced before a speed-and-capital scramble—was vivid and coherent, but CON repeatedly showed that a ticket reserve does not match the harm, does not itself produce affordability or anti-bot protection, and certainly excludes ordinary outsiders. Pressure on “or members” and on reserving even when locals already get access forced PRO to narrow the text and keep the restriction anyway; CON then offered pre-sale purchase limits and need-based seats as a way to oppose lockout without an insider queue. That was the cleaner vote path.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2: using PRO’s answers to show membership cannot do the civic work the motion allows, that lockout-prevention cannot justify a reserve even when locals already get access, and that the tools that would actually help the teacher can run before general sale without geographic ineligibility.</best_rebuttal>
